A.explanation: Point A is at $y=0$ with the same $x$ as P. P would pass through equilibrium after a quarter of a period, not after the half period elapsed at $t=1\text{ s}$.

B.explanation: After half a period P has the same $x$ but opposite displacement, moving from crest to trough. This is position B.

C.explanation: Point C has a different $x$ from P. Particles of a transverse rope wave oscillate vertically and do not travel forward with the wave.

D.explanation: Point D is a crest one wavelength ahead of P. This confuses movement of the wave pattern to the right with movement of the particle P, which stays at fixed $x$.

hints: Notice that at $t=0$ point P is at a crest of the $y$ against $x$ graph, and that a rope particle keeps the same $x$ and only moves in $y$.
Use $T=1/f$ with $f=0.5\text{ Hz}$ to find the period, then express $t=1\text{ s}$ as a fraction of that period.
Think what the displacement is after half an oscillation starting from maximum positive $y$: maximum positive, equilibrium, maximum negative.
walkthrough: At $t=0$ the diagram shows P at the top of a crest, so its displacement $y$ is $+y_{max}$ at its fixed $x$ position marked by A.
For a transverse wave the rope particles do not move in the direction of wave travel. P will oscillate up and down about $y=0$ at constant $x$.
Find the period from frequency: $T = 1/f = 1/0.5\text{ Hz} = 2.0\text{ s}$. The elapsed time is $t = 1\text{ s} = 1/2.0 = 0.5T$, so half an oscillation occurs.
Starting at a crest, a quarter period brings the particle down to $y=0$ and a further quarter period, half a period in total, brings it to the opposite extreme, the trough with $y = -y_{max}$.
That position has the same $x$ as the original P but is below the $x$-axis, which is labelled B. This is option B.
